means: Set out what the thing is, accurately and in detail. No judgement.
traversal: Breadth from one node. List its immediate neighbours: who presents it, what it presupposes, what follows from it.
structure: Define with precision. Attribute to the named scholar. Unpack the structure or steps. Quote once. Say who or what it influenced.
watch_for: Do not evaluate. Strengths and weaknesses earn nothing here and cost you time you need elsewhere.

means: Weigh the stated proposition and reach a supported judgement.
traversal: Depth along criticism chains. Each chain is attack, then defence, then your verdict.
structure: Frame the dispute. Run two or three independent chains. Order them by how decisive they are. Conclude from the verdicts, not from a summary.
watch_for: A chain that stops at the attack is description. The word 'however' should appear in every paragraph.

board_use: generic — appears in teaching and other boards
means: Break the thing into its parts and show how they relate and depend on each other.
traversal: Traverse presupposes edges. Which commitments does the position rest on, and what happens if one is removed.
structure: Identify the components. Show the dependency between them. Show what the whole rests on.
watch_for: Analysis is not description with longer sentences. If removing a part would not change the conclusion, you have not analysed.

board_use: AQA names two comparisons: Hume with Wiles, Bentham with Kant
means: Set two positions against each other on shared criteria.
traversal: A compares_with edge. Fix the criteria first, then run both positions through each one.
structure: State the criteria. Take each criterion and give both positions. End with where the deepest disagreement actually lies.
watch_for: Do not write a paragraph on one then a paragraph on the other. Interleave by criterion or it reads as two mini-essays.

traversal: Same as compare, but report only the divergences.
structure: Name the shared ground briefly, then set out where they part and why.
watch_for: Contrast without any shared ground is just two descriptions. Establish what they are both trying to answer.

means: Make the thing intelligible: how it works and why it is held.
traversal: Breadth, plus the mechanism on each edge.
structure: State the claim, give the reasoning behind it, illustrate, then say what motivates holding it.
watch_for: Explaining includes the why. A definition alone is not an explanation.

means: Give the main features concisely, without detail.
traversal: Node gloss only. Do not follow edges.
watch_for: The commonest error is writing a full Examine answer and losing time for the AO2 question.

means: Judge the worth or strength of something.
watch_for: Assess demands a verdict. A balanced survey with no conclusion caps the mark.

means: Judge how far a claim holds, expecting a qualified rather than absolute answer.
traversal: Chains, but the conclusion must be graded rather than binary.
structure: Establish the strongest case for. Establish the strongest case against. Conclude with the degree and say what it depends on.
watch_for: The phrasing invites 'partly'. Say partly in which respect, or it reads as fence-sitting.

means: Give reasons in support of a stated position.
traversal: One-sided chain: your position, the strongest objection, your response.
structure: State the position. Give the grounds. Meet the best objection.
watch_for: Justifying is not asserting. If you have not named the strongest objection, you have not justified.

means: Consider a question from more than one side and reach a view.
watch_for: Discuss still requires a conclusion. It is not permission to survey.

means: Give attention to a position and its implications.
traversal: Breadth then one hop into implications.
structure: Set out the view, then say what follows if it is true.
watch_for: Weak command word. Read the mark tariff to decide whether AO2 is wanted.
